mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and employment increase, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both series increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates during tightening cycles negatively impact S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% but returns remain positive more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPI) leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but returns are positive more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: Increased housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1.4M but returns are negative more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and employment indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If both series rise but returns are negative more than 35%.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment during late-cycle expansion signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment is low but returns are negative more than 35%.
